blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — empagliflozin across heart-failure ejection-fraction ranges
stem: A client with chronic heart failure and a left ventricular ejection fraction of 55% is prescribed empagliflozin (Jardiance). Which explanation by the nurse is most accurate?

options.A: Jardiance has a labeled heart-failure indication that is not limited to reduced ejection fraction or diabetes; trial evidence includes patients with LVEF above 40%, including 50% to under 60%.
options.B: Jardiance is appropriate for heart failure only when LVEF is 40% or lower, so an ejection fraction of 55% falls outside the population supporting heart-failure use.
options.C: Jardiance requires coexisting type 2 diabetes for its heart-failure indication because the cardiovascular benefit depends on treatment of hyperglycemia.
options.D: Jardiance is used in this setting mainly for glucose lowering and does not have a labeled indication to reduce cardiovascular death or heart-failure hospitalization.

rationale: Current JARDIANCE labeling indicates empagliflozin to reduce the risk of cardiovascular death and hospitalization for heart failure in adults with heart failure without restricting that indication to diabetes or a reduced ejection fraction. The EMPEROR-Preserved trial included adults with chronic heart failure and LVEF greater than 40%, including substantial groups with LVEF 50% to less than 60% and at least 60%, and included patients both with and without type 2 diabetes. Therefore A is correct. B, C, and D incorrectly narrow or deny the labeled heart-failure indication.
educational_objective: Recognize that empagliflozin is FDA-approved for adults with heart failure and that supporting trial evidence includes preserved-range ejection fractions and patients without diabetes.
source_version_date: DailyMed updated February 17, 2026; current label accessed 2026-08-26
source_locator: §1 Indications and Usage: reduce risk of CV death and hospitalization for heart failure in adults with heart failure. Heart Failure Trials — EMPEROR-Preserved: chronic HF NYHA II-IV with LVEF >40%; population included LVEF 50 to <60% and ≥60% and patients with and without type 2 diabetes.
source_claim_supported: Empagliflozin is FDA-labeled for adults with heart failure without a diabetes or HFrEF-only restriction; EMPEROR-Preserved included patients with LVEF above 40%, including preserved-range values.
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: evaluate medication appropriateness, provide medication education, and understand expected therapeutic outcomes.
candidate_reasons_resolved: Rewrote all four choices as complete heart-failure indication/ejection-fraction statements of comparable length.
audit_note: Independent adversarial review confirms A uniquely matches current JARDIANCE labeling and EMPEROR-Preserved evidence. No absolute cue or second defensible explanation remains.
